# px0 - Open Source Prompt, Skill & Tool Infrastructure

> Prompts, agent skills, and tools are code. Treat them like it. px0 brings versioned template management, a secure skill registry, a dynamic tool registry, and OpenTelemetry observability to your AI stack so you can iterate faster and deploy with confidence.

## Core Philosophy

Modern AI applications suffer from hardcoding logic—whether it is prompt spaghetti scattered across dozens of codebase files, raw agent tools/skills hardcoded inside application layers, or static schemas defining agent interfaces. Updating a single prompt, skill logic, or tool schema requires a git PR, code review, CI/CD run, and a service restart.

px0 decouples prompts, skills, and tools from application code:

- Prompt Registry: Prompts live as version-controlled templates.
- Skill Registry: Agent tools and functional skills live in multi-file version-controlled workspaces.
- Tool Registry: Agent tool specifications live as dynamic, version-controlled JSON schemas.
- Standardized SDKs: Applications render templates, invoke skills, and retrieve tool schemas using an ultra-simple SDK available in Python, Node.js, and Go.
- Instant Rollout: Push changes live without deploying code.
- OTEL Observability: Trace and evaluate every prompt render, skill execution, and tool schema lookup.

## Technical Features

### Self-Hosted & Private

- Flexible Deployment: Deploy px0 inside your own cloud, private VPC, or completely on-premises (air-gapped).
- Data Ownership: Retain 100% control and ownership of your prompt templates, telemetry data, and access logs.
- Compliance Ready: Meet strict security requirements like SOC2, HIPAA, and GDPR by keeping all prompt operations in-house.

### No Hardcoded Strings

- Decoupled Architecture: Prompts live in version-controlled templates, not scattered across your codebase.
- Searchability: No more nested search-and-replace to update prompt logic.

### Deploy-Free Updates

- Zero Pipeline Overhead: Push a prompt template version update and it goes live instantly.
- No Rebuilds: No git commits, pull requests, CI/CD pipelines, or container restarts are needed to update a prompt.

### Standardized SDK Integration

- Unified API signatures: Use the same patterns across Python, Node.js, and Go.
- Simple Rendering: A single render function abstracts all communication and cache-management logic.
- Flexible Configuration: Swap template names or roll out dynamic version flags without updating calling code.

### Advanced Sandboxed Templating

- Jinja Syntax: Prompts are formulated using standard Jinja2 syntax.
- Full Control: Supports advanced language constructs including variables, conditionals, loops, custom filters, and reusable macros.
- Safe Execution: Sandboxed rendering ensures untrusted inputs or bad structures never crash the main application.

### Atomic Versioning and Rollbacks

- Immutable Revisions: Every published prompt template version is immutable.
- Atomic Deployments: Changes are rolled out atomically across all active SDK instances.
- Instant Recovery: Roll back to any previous healthy template version in one click.

### Team-Level RBAC

- Granular Access Control: Define role-based access controls for developers, reviewers, and publishers.
- Team Permissions: Manage template access and modification rights across different engineering teams.
- Granular Policies: Fine-grained permissions on who can view, edit, draft, or publish prompt templates.

### Draft and Review Workflows

- Lifecycle Management: Draft, review, and publish cycles ensure that prompt revisions undergo checks.
- Comparison Tooling: Interactive visual diffs between any two template versions.
- Change Tracking: Detailed log of every change capturing what was modified, by whom, and when.

### Native OpenTelemetry Observability

- Built-In Tracing: Every prompt rendering is traced and measured natively.
- Standard Exporters: Supports out-of-the-box exporting for latency, performance, and render error metrics.
- Multi-Backend Integration: Send tracing spans and metric data to any standard OpenTelemetry collector or backend.

### Skill Registry & Workspace Files

- Multi-File Workspaces: Every skill version maintains a complete, structured file tree. Edit files in-place or upload/download ZIP packages of your logic.
- Flexible Asset Handling: Read, write, or delete individual code assets within draft skill versions before promotion.

### Skill Version Promotion Pipelines

- Safe Lifecycle States: Manage skills using distinct operational states: `draft` -> `stable` -> `live`.
- Safe Iteration: Only `draft` versions can be modified or deleted. Stable and live versions are immutable.
- Dynamic Duplication: Create new draft iterations by duplicating any version's file tree in one click.

### Skill Template Rendering

- Dynamic Code Templating: Render skill source/configuration templates dynamically prior to execution.
- Sandboxed Jinja Support: Securely inject real-time system context, active parameters, or environment variables into your tool/skill execution context.

### Tool Registry & JSON Schema Definitions

- Input & Output Schemas: Define exact JSON Schema structures for tool inputs and outputs. Ensure full validation of parameters and returned results.
- LLM Discovery Ready: Expose structured tool metadata and descriptions so that LLM orchestration systems can discover and invoke tools dynamically.

### Tool Version Promotion Pipelines

- Immutable Schema Versions: Promoting tool schemas from `draft` to `stable` makes them immutable. No more downstream drift or accidental API updates.
- Automatic Demotion on Promotion: Promoting a tool version to `live` automatically demotes any previous active version to `stable`. Roll back atomically with a single API request.

## SDK Integration Examples

Below are standard examples demonstrating how a Jinja template is set up and rendered across various backend SDKs.

### Prompt Template: customer_support.j2

```jinja
{# customer_support - v7 #}
{% set tone = "formal" if user.tier == "enterprise" else "friendly" %}

You are a {{ tone }} assistant for {{ company.name }}.
User: {{ query }}
Lang: {{ lang | default("English") }}
```

### Python SDK Usage

```python
import px0

# Render the prompt template directly
prompt = px0.render("customer_support", {
    "user": user,
    "company": company,
    "query": query,
})
```

### Node.js SDK Usage

```typescript
import { px0 } from "px0";

// Render prompt template asynchronously
const prompt = await px0.render("customer_support", {
  user,
  company,
  query,
});
```

### Go SDK Usage

```go
import "github.com/px0-ai/px0-go"

// Render the prompt template using maps
prompt, err := px0.Render("customer_support",
    map[string]any{
        "user":    user,
        "company": company,
        "query":   query,
    },
)
```

### Skill Execution SDK Usage

Invoke and run skills from the registry dynamically using simple, unified SDK methods across languages:

#### Python SDK Usage

```python
# Execute a live skill by slug
result = px0.execute_skill(
    slug="data_analyzer",
    version="live",
    input={"data": [1, 2, 3]}
)
```

#### Node.js SDK Usage

```typescript
// Execute a live skill by slug
const result = await px0.executeSkill("data_analyzer", {
  version: "live",
  input: { data: [1, 2, 3] }
});
```

#### Go SDK Usage

```go
// Execute a live skill by slug
res, _, _ := client.SkillsAPI.
  Execute(nil, "data_analyzer").
  Version("live").
  Input(map[string]interface{}{
    "data": []int{1, 2, 3},
  }).
  Execute()
```
